question.text: A mass <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>9</mn><mo> </mo><mi>kg</mi></math>, attached to a horizontal spring, executes SHM with an amplitude <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math>. When this mass passes through its mean position, then a smaller mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>124</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> is placed over it and both masses move together with amplitude <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math>. If the ratio <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><msub><mi>A</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></mfrac></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><mi>α</mi><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></mfrac></math>, then the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>α</mi></math> will be _____ .

solution.text:
At mean position, the velocity of the particle in S.H.M. is maximum, so kinetic energy is KE=12kA2, where, k is spring constant.

We also know that, kinetic energy is related to momentum as KE=p22m.

Now, from both equations, we have 

12kA2=p22m     (Here, momentum is conserved)

⇒A1 A22=m2 m1=1024900

⇒A1 A2=3230=1615=1616-1

∴α=16
